decisions.reason: As a flagship harvesting crate tied to the firm's sustainability direction, it carries strategic aspiration value, and the large firm's slack allows time for results to mature.
A multi-model foldable large container line with its own page fits the core returnable-packaging business, and nothing signals a shortfall that would trigger problemistic search.
Stackable crates are core standard products with broad demand across food and retail, so cutting the line soon after launch is unlikely.
A medium-duty rackable pallet line complements the pallet portfolio and has low incremental cost, so it likely meets aspirations.
The spill-retention pallet serves an industrial niche, but with its own page and several models it shows commitment, and slack lets the firm carry it.
It is a single-model niche pallet with a dedicated page, and one year of evidence is too little to judge it below aspiration, so it is kept for now.
